newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks rise on stronger Dow, metals.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks rise on stronger Dow, metals.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.205 +0.025 Gold 342.40/90 Lon fix 343.75
*Stocks quickly regain most of Thursday's losses on stronger Dow and metal prices. Vol 54.03 million, value A$166.16 million, 470 stocks traded, 189 steady, 221 up, 70 down.

Australian stocks quickly regained most of Thursday's losses at the opening on Friday after a rebound on Wall Street and with resources well-supported after stronger metal prices and firmer bullion and oil prices.
The All Ordinaries index was 9.4 points up at 2,514.1 at 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT). It closed 12.9 points down on Thursday.
June share price index futures were seven points up at 2,522, with the premium to the physical index at 7.9 points.
Brokers said the market was likely to trade in a narrow range with few local issues around today and with investors setting their positions ahead of the weekend.
"It is pretty subdued at the moment. I don't think there is anything standing out," said one Melbourne-based broker.
Brokers said ICI Australia was steady after sliding about nine percent on Thursday after its British parent ICI Plc unveiled plans to sell its stake, worth around A$2 billion.

Market leader BHP topped the turnover charts with over A$100 million worth of trade. The stock went ex-div on Thursday. The resource giant announced plans after Thursday's market close for a A$636 million share issue.
Traders said oil stocks continued their recent rally buoyed by sharp gains in U.S. cash crude prices.
Gold and base metal miners shares were also well-supported after strong gains in metal prices on the LME and higher gold futures in New York.
Banks were broadly firmer, continuing their recent gains ahead of a new round of interim results. National Australia Bank and Westpac both report next week.
In other market news, Australian bonds showed modest yield falls in early trading, but interest was thin as the market caught its breath after the whippy price action this week.
At 10.55 a.m. (0055 GMT), the 10 year T-bond yield was four basis points lower at 7.76 percent.

The Australian dollar reclaimed US$0.7800 as the offshore reacted more favourably than locals to the hawkish testimony on Thursday of RBA governor Ian Macfarlane, which all but ruled out a cut in official rates.
At 11.05 a.m. (0105 GMT), the dollar was trading at US$0.7802/07, compared with around US$0.7776/81 in late local trading on Thursday.
